metadata.title: Dirac eigenvalue comparison
metadata.abstract: We study how curvature bounds control the Dirac eigenvalues of closed spin manifolds, comparing the positive and negative eigenvalues separately. Within a fixed conformal class and spin structure, pointwise ordering of scalar curvature relative to a metric of negative scalar curvature implies comparison at every nonzero index. On the two-sphere, a holomorphic ladder on the half-canonical bundle proves the corresponding comparison in both directions under a Gaussian curvature bound. On surfaces of higher genus, the same bundle identities propagate comparison from the scalar and spinor levels to higher canonical powers. In the round conformal class on the higher dimensional sphere, a prescribed scalar curvature bound yields an upper bound in absolute value for the first $2^{[n/2]}$ Dirac eigenvalues. When the conformal class varies, we can show that the corresponding comparisons on hyperbolic surfaces and odd-dimensional spheres no longer hold; while on even-dimensional spheres, the first gap and all sufficiently high-index eigenvalues of either sign satisfy a one-direction comparison.
